before.statement: Thomson acknowledged Clausius’s proof of the reversible-engine proposition, attributed one foundational proposition jointly to Carnot and Clausius, and compared their heat-flow axioms.

evidence.locator: Transactions §§9 and 14, including the paragraph beginning with Clausius priority and Thomson’s independent-proof statement
evidence.supports: Explicit acknowledgment and comparison; explicit limit on a claimed invention channel.

before.alternatives: Thomson says his own demonstration occurred before he knew Clausius’s proof.
before.uncertainty: This edge records incorporation, credit and comparison in the presented theory; it does not say Clausius caused Thomson to invent his proof. The precise source event is unresolved: Thomson dates the published second-part proof to May 1850, while the 1867 Clausius collection gives March–April. The February communication is not established as the source of that proof.
before.temporal_note: Clausius’s 1850 work precedes acknowledged use in 1851; Thomson’s claimed independent conception is kept separate.

provenance.note: The stated claim is supported by the identified passages; historical and lifecycle acceptance are assessed separately.

before.statement: Thomson adopted Joule’s refined mechanical equivalent as a numerical input to his dynamical heat-engine calculations.

evidence.supports: Explicit quotation of Joule’s preferred 772.69 figure and use in the calculations.

before.alternatives: Thomson also discussed Rankine’s rounded value and combined the equivalent with separate experimental data.
before.uncertainty: Thomson describes a 32–33 °F thermal unit while Joule’s conclusion specifies water near 55–60 °F; this historical convention mismatch is retained as a limit, not silently corrected.
before.temporal_note: 1849 communication/1850 publication precede the March 1851 presentation.
